stories.title: TCL says its OLED inkjet printing process has reached the point of "stable mass production"
stories.description: In July, we reported that TCL CSOT has began to commercially produce consumer inkjet printed OLED panels, for laptops and monitors. The company has now announced that its inkjet printing process has reached the point of "stable mass production".TCL CSOT already announced it is starting mass production at its 5.5-Gen inkjet printed OLED line towards the end of 2024, but these were panels that target the medical market, that were produced at a very low volume. The company is now ramping up production for consumer products, at higher levels. TCL's first panels are produced at the company's 5.5-Gen pilot line. The company's T8 large-scale 8.6-Gen line is not ready for production yet. Several companies already launched products based on TCL CSOT's new IJP panels, including the premium MSI Pro Max OLED 271UPJW12 monitor, based on a 27" 4K (164 PPI 120Hz panel, the Lenovo's Legion R9000P gaming laptop and the Lenovo ThinkVision P27UL-40 laptop, which uses the same 27" 4K panel as MSI's monitor.While the 5.5-Gen pilot line in Wuhan has a limited capacity, CSOT recently announced it plans to triple its capacity, in a $211 million investment. This new capacity will be ready by 2028. This will still be a low volume line, even after the expansion. Once CSOT's 8.6-Gen inkjet printing line is ready (which will be at around 2027 or 2028), the company will utilize the 5.5-Gen line mostly for R&D, pilot production and verification of products on a pilot scale. The 5.5-Gen line is based on equipment that TCL CSOT acquired from JOLED, after it was bankrupt in 2023.
